The phone is always masked in this list; the full number is on callbacks_get. Needs the RingTonic integration on. While contact details are not stored in Full, names come back empty.

status.description: Which callbacks: open (default: open, returned, follow_up), closed (done, not_lead, expired), all (every status, held included), one status, or a comma list of statuses.

page.description: Page number, 1 to 10000 (default 1); above 10000 is 422 invalid_page.

per_page.description: Rows per page, 1 to 200 (default 50); a value outside that range is clamped to it, not refused.

operations.summary: One callback with its recent history: at most the 50 most recent events, including calls both ways: outbound (kinds outbound_completed, outbound_missed, outbound_recording, outbound_transcription, outbound_placed) and inbound (inbound_completed, inbound_missed, inbound_recording, inbound_transcription; history only, an inbound call never changes the status). Each call event carries event, call status, duration, when, and the AI summary only while contact details are stored in Full; an inbound call also carries caller_name (the caller-ID name the carrier gives, normalized; Full only); never a transcript or a recording link. A contact_edited event (a person edited the contact in the portal, or the AI read filled a field: source ai) carries the field names in changed, the source and via, never the values. The AI read of a call transcript (v1.6.781) adds three kinds: ai_read (one per call: state queued, running, done or skipped with why such as daily_limit, the outcome, confidence and pct, the follow_up_date, decision {kind apply, suggest or none, why}, applied {from, to}, suggest {action, status_at}, contact_fill field names; reason, quote, contact_suggest and cnam only while contact details are stored in Full), ai_status (the status change the AI made: from, to, outcome, confidence, pct, read; reason and quote Full only; actor ai) and ai_dismissed (read, part status or contact; actor the person). `ai` (Full only, else {}) is what the portal row shows now: label {kind opened or closed, to, reason, pct, at}, suggest {read, action done, not_lead or reopen, reason, pct, text}, contact {read, fields {field: {value, source transcript or cnam}}, cnam, text}, skipped {why, text}. Returns the full phone only while contact details are stored in Full; otherwise the masked number and an empty name (the stored row is kept, not shown).
operations.returns: data: {id, phone? (Full only), phone_masked, status, reason, display_name, carry_since, follow_up_date, follow_up_owner, closed_by, closed_at, last_lead_id, created_at, updated_at, events[] (at most 50, newest first): {kind, actor, at, payload{source?, lead_id?, status?, action?, from?, to?, via?, api_key?, event?, duration?, call_log_uuid?, started_at?, recording?, transcription_confidence?, summary? (Full only), caller_name? (inbound, Full only), changed? (contact_edited: field names), state?, why?, error?, direction?, attempts?, outcome?, confidence?, pct?, follow_up_date?, decision?, applied?, suggest?, contact_fill?, read?, part? (AI read events), reason?, quote?, contact_suggest?, cnam? (AI, Full only)}}, ai {label?, suggest?, contact?, skipped?} (Full only)}

operations.summary: Mark a callback done or not a lead, or reopen a closed one, recorded against a named person (their people slug) and the time. `do` is the verb. An API-key call must name the person with exactly one of `actor` (people slug) or `as_user_id` (WordPress user id); a signed-in SyteOps Admin who names nobody acts as themselves. A slug is accepted only while it belongs to the current holder of its Users slot (422 actor_not_current). 422 actor_unresolved answers an unknown actor slug, an as_user_id with no people-registry entry, and a signed-in SyteOps Admin with no registry entry who names nobody; sending both actor and as_user_id is 422 actor_required. 403 actor_not_permitted when the Callbacks access of that person does not allow acting. A second request on an already-handled callback, or reopen on a callback that is not closed, changes nothing and says who acted and when (changed:false, already:true). Refused 422 invalid_action for any other `do`, 404 not_found for an unknown id, 409 state_changed when the callback moved under two attempts, 409 contact_details_not_full while contact details are not stored in Full, 409 callbacks_disabled when the RingTonic integration is off, 409 module_unavailable while Lead Attribution is off, and 409 in_flight while the same request is still being applied.

do.description: done, not_lead or reopen (reopen applies only to a done, not_lead or expired callback).

actor.description: People slug of the person acting; must be a current slot holder.

as_user_id.description: WordPress user id of the person acting, resolved to their people slug. Use instead of actor.

operations.returns: data: {id, action, status, already, message, by, by_label? (already only), at}; changed is false when already is true

operations.summary: Read the Leads settings as the code uses them (the effective value `wp syteops leads setting get` prints), with each key's type, whether it may be written, and whether it is masked. A webhook address (masked) reads '' when empty and '[set]' otherwise; it is never returned. pii_mode is the mode in force, through the syteops_leads_pii_mode filter the contact-details writers apply. `notes` names a key stored in an older shape, or the stored pii_mode when a filter overrides it. Never returns a RingTonic secret (they are not settings).

keys.description: Only these setting keys (default: all). An entry that is not a string is 422 invalid_params; an unknown key is 422 unknown_setting.

operations.returns: data: {settings: {key: value}, keys: {key: {type, writable, masked, egress, confirm}}, notes: {key: note}}. egress: the key decides where lead data is sent. confirm: changing it on leads.settings_set needs confirm: true (pii_mode, ringtonic_store_call_summary and every egress key; ringtonic_contact_internal only when set to push).

operations.summary: Set one or more Leads settings in one write, all or nothing, with the settings screen's own rule for each key (the same table `wp syteops leads setting set` uses): a value the screen would quietly correct is refused. Keys are applied in the screen's order, so consent_mode lands before consent_cookie. Refused with 422 and nothing written: an unknown key (unknown_setting), ringtonic_noabort (screen_only_setting: it edits .htaccess), a RingTonic secret by any name (secret_setting: secrets are never written through this API; set them from a terminal with `wp syteops systems-api set --stdin`), a value the rules refuse (invalid_setting). A change to pii_mode (how contact details are stored) or to a key that decides where lead contact details are sent (crm_webhook_url, automation_webhook_url, recipient_emails, email_reply_to, callbacks_summary_slots, callbacks_reminder_slots, callbacks_weekly_slots, callbacks_reminders_enabled), or turns on a switch that sends lead details off-site (automation_webhook_enabled, crm_webhook_enabled, email_instant_enabled, email_periodic_enabled, ringtonic_contact_forms, ringtonic_contact_field_names, ringtonic_contact_internal=push), or changes ringtonic_store_call_summary, needs confirm:true (409 confirmation_required, naming the keys); resending the current value does not. The confirm is one explicit step for every caller, not a role check. changed is false and nothing is written when no stored value would change.

settings.description: A non-empty object of {setting: value}; see settings_get for the keys and types. Lists and maps are JSON values.

confirm.description: true to change pii_mode, ringtonic_store_call_summary, a lead-data destination (the two webhook addresses, recipient_emails, email_reply_to, callbacks_summary_slots, callbacks_reminder_slots, callbacks_weekly_slots, callbacks_reminders_enabled) or an off-site switch (automation_webhook_enabled, crm_webhook_enabled, email_instant_enabled, email_periodic_enabled, ringtonic_contact_forms, ringtonic_contact_field_names, ringtonic_contact_internal=push).

operations.returns: data: {changed_keys[], settings: {key: value} (the keys sent, effective, masked keys as '' or '[set]')}

operations.summary: Issue (or return) the people link of the person in a Users slot: the stable slug a callback closure and a call are credited to. user_num.description: Slot number, one to three digits, for example 007 or 7.

operations.returns: data: {user_num, slug, name, issued (true when this call created the slug)}

Read the Content Pipelines operating mode: setup or production. Setup still ingests and builds posts, but forces newly ingested posts to draft, writes no run-history rows, skips the workflow forward and the new-post reviewer email, holds social sends until production, and skips the 'Now live', schedule-change and held-source alert emails. The Review Portal stays fully usable: setup mode does NOT stop review.approve or calendar publishing.

Switch the Content Pipelines mode. Production lets ingested posts take their source's configured status and turns on run history, the workflow forward, social sends and the pipeline emails. Setup still ingests and builds posts, but forces newly ingested posts to draft, writes no run-history rows, skips the workflow forward and the new-post reviewer email, holds social sends until production, and skips the 'Now live', schedule-change and held-source alert emails. The Review Portal stays fully usable: setup mode does NOT stop review.approve or calendar publishing. Needs confirm:true. Any other mode value is 422 invalid_mode.

Destructive: it creates or updates the article with the source's own settings, so a source set to publish publishes it, a source in overwrite mode overwrites reviewer edits on an article already live, and the draft core spends an AI call. Shares the source's daily AI allowance (default 10 a day, UTC) with learn_from_sample.
operations.returns: data: {outcome, message, post_id, created, edit_link}; changed is false for a held or protected article. 404 not_found (unknown or disabled source), 409 confirmation_required or no_payload, 422 invalid_json, 429 learn_cap_reached

operations.summary: Ask the Ingest AI area to propose a field mapping from the source's captured sample. Spends an AI call and shares the source's daily AI allowance (default 10 a day, UTC) with reprocess.

confirm.description: Required (true) when the source's mapping is approved.

operations.returns: data: {mapping}; changed is true. 404 not_found, 409 confirmation_required, no_provider or no_sample, 422 invalid_sample, 429 learn_cap_reached, 502 ai_empty_response or invalid_json, 503 ai_unavailable

Recompute the agent-prompt guard hash (CANON-1) for one Elementor element so a session can compare it before writing. Returns the hash and its key list only, never a setting value.
Read one post's SEO title, description and focus keywords from whichever SEO tool is active. With no active SEO tool it returns 409 no_active_seo_tool.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, tool, tool_label, fields: {title, description, keywords}}

operations.summary: Write one post's SEO title, description or focus keywords through the active SEO tool's own writer. Use this, not update_content meta, for every SEO plugin. dry_run:true writes nothing and returns each field's current and proposed value; a real write returns 409 confirmation_required until confirm:true. Only the fields sent change; any other field is refused. Caps: title 300, description 1000, keywords 500 characters. A placeholder the SEO tool fills from site data is refused (422 seo_token_not_allowed) unless allow_placeholders:true.

title.description: SEO title. Send an empty string to clear it.

description.description: Meta description. Send an empty string to clear it.

keywords.description: Focus keywords, comma-separated. Send an empty string to clear it.

allow_placeholders.description: JSON true only. Allow placeholders the SEO tool fills from site data (custom fields, options). Off by default; only safe ones such as the post title are accepted without it.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, tool, tool_label, dry_run, changed, written, fields: {<field>: {current, proposed, changed}}, placeholders: {<field>: []}, stored?: {title, description, keywords}, note?}

operations.summary: Purge one post's page (post_id), or up to 30 URLs on this site's own host (urls), from LiteSpeed and Cloudflare when present. With post_id it also asks Elementor to rebuild its generated CSS when that post is built with Elementor. Send post_id or urls, not both; a URL on any other host refuses the whole call.

urls.description: List of absolute http(s) URLs on this site's host, at most 30.

operations.returns: data: {urls[], purged[], attempted[], skipped[], errors[], elementor_css: cleared|unavailable|not_elementor|null}

operations.summary: One page of a person's Review Portal queue, as that person sees it. list is pending (default), watching, live, live_posts, live_pages, coming_up or notes. An API-key call must send as_user_id (the person whose queue to read; 422 as_user_id_required otherwise, 404 user_not_found when no such user); a signed-in SyteOps Admin defaults to themselves. per_page is 5, 10, 25 or 100. Page with the returned next_cursor. No review links are returned.

list.description: pending (default), watching, live, live_posts, live_pages, coming_up or notes.

operations.returns: data: {as_user_id, list, rows[], has_more, next_cursor, truncated, page_count}; a post row is {post_id, title, source, received, scheduled_ts, modified_ts, feedback_count, changes_requested, qa}, a notes row is {post_id, title, author, excerpt, created, note_id}

operations.summary: One post's review status: post status, whether changes are requested, open and total note counts, the reviewers and watchers, and the latest recorded activity. A missing, trashed or non-viewable post is 404 post_not_found.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, title, post_status, changes_requested, open_notes, total_notes, reviewers[], watchers[], last_activity: {event, at}|null}; a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: The people who may review one post and the people watching it. Ids, display names and roles only; no email addresses.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, reviewers[], watchers[]}; a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: One post's review notes and replies, oldest first, as the portal shows them. per_page is 1 to 100 (default 25).
operations.returns: data: {post_id, total, page, per_page, has_more, comments[]}; a comment is {id, parent, user_id, user_name, note, created_at, kind, target_kind, att_id, resolved, via_api}; via_api is true for a note written through this API

operations.summary: Add a reviewer to one post, as the portal's Send to a colleague does: the person is emailed that they were asked to help review, the post's review link gets a fresh expiry window, and the post's activity log records it. Adding a reviewer lets that person open and edit the post, and publish it when who_can_publish is any. Under who_can_publish=author_approver they can edit but not publish, unless they are the post's author or a site administrator or SyteOps Admin. user_id must be a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account (422 user_not_selectable; 404 user_not_found when no such account). A post that was never sent for review is refused (409 not_review_managed). A watcher who is added as a reviewer stops being a watcher. Someone already listed is ok with changed:false and is not emailed again.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, user_id, emailed, notify: {outcome: sent|queued|failed|off|none, partial}, reviewers[], watchers[]}; emailed and notify only when the person was added; a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: Remove a reviewer from one post: they can no longer open, edit or publish it through the portal (unless they are a site administrator, or a watcher or a bundle reviewer of it, which keeps that narrower access), and their queued review emails for it are dropped when they no longer have any access. The post's author stays on the list (409 author_protected). The removal sticks: the post's source default reviewers and CCs do not put them back. Someone not listed is ok with changed:false. No email is sent; the activity log records it.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]} (the lists after the call); a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: Add a watcher to one post: they may open it and comment, and receive its routine review emails, but cannot edit or publish it. user_id must be a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account (422 user_not_selectable). A post that was never sent for review is refused (409 not_review_managed). A reviewer of the post is refused (409 already_reviewer). Someone already watching is ok with changed:false. No email is sent; the activity log records it.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]} (the lists after the call); a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: Remove a watcher from one post: they can no longer open or comment on it unless something else grants that, and their queued review emails for it are then dropped. The removal sticks: the post's source default CCs do not put them back. Someone not watching is ok with changed:false. No email is sent; the activity log records it.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]} (the lists after the call); a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}

operations.summary: Approve a post for publishing, as the Review Portal's Publish does with nothing edited: it publishes now, or schedules it when the post holds a reviewer's intended time or a reserved cadence slot at least a minute ahead and scheduling is on. A post already scheduled keeps its own date: with scheduling on and the date at least a minute ahead it is ok with changed:false and already_scheduled:true, and nothing is written, logged or emailed; with scheduling off that date could not be kept, so it is refused (409 scheduling_off; unschedule it first to publish now). A scheduled date already due (a missed schedule) publishes with that date. Acts with admin authority: an admin or API-key caller bypasses the post's reviewer list and the who_can_publish rule, which gate people in the portal, and is limited to posts in review. It records the approver as user 0 whenever the API key authorized the call, otherwise the signed-in SyteOps Admin. A post never sent for review (no reviewers and no review link) is refused (409 not_in_review). A post already live is ok with changed:false and already_live:true, and nothing is written, logged or emailed. A title, excerpt or body the call does not send is published exactly as stored. Every portal check applies: 409 not_ready (with failed[] requirements), 409 published_immutable, 500 publish_failed. Open notes do not block it (the portal only warns); open_notes reports them. Destructive: send confirm:true.

confirm.description: Must be true: this puts a post live.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, status, scheduled, scheduled_readable, permalink, emailed, notify: {outcome, partial}, images: {imported, reused, failed, capped}|null, open_notes, approved_by: {user_id, via, api_key}, already_live, already_scheduled}

operations.summary: Send a post back for changes as one person, as the Review Portal's Request Changes does: records message as their note, cancels a pending schedule when they may publish, and emails the author and co-reviewers. The note is marked as added via API, and the portal's history says so. An API-key call must send as_user_id; a signed-in SyteOps Admin defaults to themselves. That person must be able to edit the post in the portal (403 forbidden); 409 schedule_due when it is about to publish and they cannot cancel it.

message.description: The note, plain text, up to the portal's note length.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, as_user_id, entry: {id, parent, kind, created_at, via_api}, emailed, notify: {outcome, partial}, unscheduled, status}

operations.summary: Add a review note as one person, through the Review Portal's own writer, so the notes email batches it the same way. Send exactly one target: parent_id (a reply to a top-level note; notify and resolve apply), attachment_id or image_url (a note on a picture), or element (a note pinned to a page element, with the portal's element fields such as selector, text and heading). The portal has no untargeted note; use request_changes for an article-level note. The note is marked as added via API, and the portal's history says so. An API-key call must send as_user_id; that person must be able to comment on the post (403 forbidden), and resolve needs edit rights.

parent_id.description: Reply to this top-level note id.

notify.description: Reply only: email the thread (default true).

resolve.description: Reply only: also resolve the parent note.

image_url.description: The picture's URL, when it has no attachment id.

element.description: Element target: selector, sig, text, ox, oy, vw, media, src, name, breakpoint, bp_px, tag, el_id, classes, heading, html, builder_path, rect, url, bld.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, as_user_id, kind: reply|image|element, entry: {id, parent, kind, created_at, via_api}}; a reply adds {resolve: changed|unchanged|missing|failed|null (null when not asked), notified, notify: {outcome, partial}}

operations.summary: The Review Portal's Portal Permissions as the settings screen reads them: who_can_publish (any or author_approver) and the per-area matrix, with a default row (everyone else), role rows keyed by SyteOps role slug and person rows keyed by user number. An absent role or person cell inherits; an absent default cell is that area's default. Also lists every area with its allowed values and whether this site's screen shows it, and the role and person rows that may be set (a person is listed only when linked to a WordPress account, as on the screen). A SyteOps Admin is never restricted by the matrix, and site administrators can always publish. Works before the portal is in use.
operations.returns: data: {who_can_publish, permissions: {default: {area: value}, roles: {slug: {area: value}}, users: {user_num: {area: value}}}, areas[]: {key, label, values[], default, shown}, roles[]: {slug, name}, users[]: {user_num, name}}

operations.summary: Change who can review and publish in the Review Portal. Partial: only the cells sent change, every other cell and row is kept. In roles and users a cell of inherit (or null) clears it and a row of null clears the whole row; the default row takes real values only. Every section, role slug, user number (a person linked to a WordPress account, as the screen lists), area and value is checked against the settings screen's own lists, and an area the screen does not show on this site is refused (422 invalid_permissions; nothing is written). who_can_publish is any or author_approver (422 invalid_who_can_publish). Switching to author_approver when no user holds the administrator publish override is refused (409 no_publisher_left). Send at least one of the two (422 nothing_to_change). One set runs at a time; a concurrent one is refused (409 busy) rather than risk losing a cell, so retry it. Saved through the screen's own validator and recorded in the activity log. Requires confirm:true.

permissions.description: Partial matrix: {default?: {area: value}, roles?: {slug: {area: value|inherit|null}|null}, users?: {user_num: {area: value|inherit|null}|null}}.

who_can_publish.description: any (any selected reviewer) or author_approver (the post author or an administrator).

operations.returns: data: {who_can_publish, permissions: {default, roles, users} as stored after the change, changes[]: {row, area, from, to}} (null = unset)

operations.summary: The publishing calendar for a window: scheduled and published posts in it (grid_events) plus the undated draft and pending rail. from and to are ISO 8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD: whole days) or date-times, in the site timezone unless they carry Z or an offset, and the window may span at most 92 days (422 range_too_large). scope is pipeline (default, posts the content pipeline produced) or all. post_types, when sent, must be a list of calendar post types. grid_truncated is true when the window held more posts than the grid returns (500): narrow the window. The rail is not date-bounded: page it with rail_cursor and rail_per (5, 10, 25 or 100). A site-local time that the clocks skip is 422 date_in_dst_gap.

from.description: Window start: YYYY-MM-DD (start of that day) or an ISO 8601 date-time.

to.description: Window end: YYYY-MM-DD (end of that day) or an ISO 8601 date-time. At most 92 days after from.

post_types.description: A JSON list of calendar post type names, e.g. ["post", "page"]; a keyed object is refused.

rail_cursor.description: rail_next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged; anything else is 422 invalid_cursor.

operations.returns: data: {from_gmt, to_gmt, scope, grid_events[], grid_truncated, rail_drafts[], rail_has_more, rail_next_cursor, rail_truncated}; an event is {id, title, type, type_label, status, date_gmt, date_site, reserved, pipeline_origin}

operations.summary: Move a post's publication to a future moment, exactly as dragging it on the calendar does: a draft or pending post becomes scheduled, a scheduled post moves, and the schedule notice goes to the people the portal tells. date must be at least five minutes ahead (422 date_not_future), and the post is never published instead; a live post cannot be given a later date (409 published_immutable). A bad date is 422 invalid_date.

date.description: ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00 (site timezone) or 2026-11-03T09:00:00Z / +02:00 (that instant).

operations.returns: data: {post_id, status, scheduled, intent, date_gmt, date_site, notify}; notify is the schedule notice outcome

operations.summary: Cancel a scheduled post's publication and return it to a draft (409 not_scheduled when it is not scheduled). Reversible: the cancelled moment is returned as previous_gmt and reschedule puts it back.

Take a LIVE post down and return it to a draft (409 not_published when it is not live). The site's static front page and posts page are refused (409 protected_page). The publication date is kept; pending post-publish recipe runs and social sends are stood down. Destructive: send confirm:true.

The next free publishing moment on the site's cadence after a time (default now). enabled is false and the slot empty when cadence is off; truncated means the walk could not read the calendar completely. exclude_post_id keeps that post out of its own conflicts. scope is all (default) or pipeline.

after.description: ISO 8601 date-time to search after (default now).

operations.returns: data: {enabled, truncated, slot_gmt, slot_site}; the slot strings are empty when none

operations.summary: Would scheduling this post at this moment break the site's publishing rhythm, and where would it fit instead? Advisory: nothing is written or refused. scope is all (default) or pipeline.

date.description: ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00 (site timezone) or 2026-11-03T09:00:00Z / +02:00 (that instant).

operations.returns: data: {post_id, date_gmt, enabled, collides, reasons[], conflicts[], suggestion_label, suggestion_local, truncated}

operations.summary: Hold the next free cadence moment on a draft or pending post, as an arriving article gets one (a post already holding one is moved). Only a draft or pending post can hold a slot (409 not_holdable), and only a post type the calendar handles (422 unsupported_type). Not reserving is an answer: reserved is false with a reason of slots_disabled, cadence_opt_out or not_reserved.

Queue one social send for one article to a configured destination. when is time (default; send at fire_at, a Unix time in seconds between one minute and five years ahead) or on_publish (send when the article first goes live; fire_at not allowed). text is the final post text, up to 3000 characters (counted as characters, not bytes). A signed-in caller also needs publish capability for the post type (403 forbidden), as in the screen; a key skips that check. Refuses 409 social_disabled while Social Publishing is off, 422 bad_destination for an unknown destination_id, and 404 post_not_found for a missing, trashed or non-viewable post.

text.description: The final post text, up to 3000 characters.

fire_at.label: a Unix time in seconds
fire_at.description: Unix time in seconds; required when when is time.

operations.returns: data: {post_id, job_id, when, fire_at, destination: {id, name}}

operations.summary: Cancel one scheduled social send on an article, by the job_id social.schedule returned. Works while Social Publishing is off, so a pending send can always be stopped. 404 post_not_found for a missing, trashed or non-viewable post (trashing a post already drops its scheduled sends); 404 job_not_found when no such job is pending.

Build the listing-card image for each image the article owns that lacks a current one (the same unforced path a page render takes; images already current are left alone). With the repair on this queues paid jobs. At most 25 images per call. 409 listing_image_disabled when the feature is off; 429 cooldown (10 minutes per article, shared with reprocess, released when nothing was built or queued); 429 daily_limit when the site-wide daily allowance of images (100 by default, counted per image across run and reprocess, refunded when nothing was built or queued) is used up; processed and queued count only images built or newly queued, and changed is true only then; 404 post_not_found for a missing, trashed or non-viewable post.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, processed, queued, failed, skipped, items[] is {attachment_id, built, queued, error?, repaired?, reason?, retrying?}}

operations.summary: Rebuild the listing-card image for each image the article owns, from scratch, even when one looks current: the failure memo is cleared and the repair is re-queued (paid). The live crop stays until the new one replaces it, so this is not destructive. At most 25 images per call; same refusals, 10-minute per-article cooldown and site-wide daily image allowance as run.
operations.returns: data: {post_id, processed, queued, failed, skipped, items[] is {attachment_id, built, queued, error?, repaired?, reason?, retrying?}}

operations.summary: Read the site time zone (WordPress Settings, General). It decides when a callback follow-up is due today and the times the portal shows. city is true for a region zone such as America/Detroit; note recommends one otherwise.

Set the site time zone the way the General settings screen stores a city zone (timezone_string set, gmt_offset emptied). One identifier from PHP's timezone_identifiers_list(): a city zone such as America/Detroit is recommended (daylight saving follows it); UTC is accepted; a raw offset (UTC+5), a backward-compatible alias (US/Eastern) or anything else is 422 invalid_timezone and nothing changes. The offset is emptied only after the zone is read back (a save that did not stick is 500 write_failed and leaves both as they were). A changed zone re-arms the events pinned to a site-time hour (the 02:00 FlowMattic orphan sweep).

timezone_string.description: A time zone identifier, for example America/Detroit.
